name: US inflation
summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September; October data due mid-November
state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7%, within the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). Brent fell to about $94 on 4 Nov, near a three-week low, on hopes of a US–Iran deal, which may ease energy inflation if sustained. October CPI is due mid-November.
for_you: Prices are rising faster than the Fed's 2% target, squeezing real incomes. Fuel and energy costs are the main swing factor in coming months.
why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
